musango:table:1.title: 2026 in archosaur paleontology (table of new taxa)

musango:study:1.title: A new sauropodomorph dinosaur from the Pebbly Arkose Formation (Upper Triassic: Norian) of Kariba, Zimbabwe (Journal of Systematic Palaeontology, 2026)

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was discovered in March 2018 on the margin of Lake Kariba by a South African and Zimbabwean-led expedition.
facts.quote: It was discovered in March 2018 on the margin of Lake Kariba by a South African/Zimbabwean-led expedition

facts.statement: The specimen is housed in the Natural History Museum of Zimbabwe in Bulawayo under the accession code NHMZ 2583.
facts.quote: and is permanently accessioned in the Natural History Museum of Zimbabwe in Bulawayo, Zimbabwe, under the code NHMZ 2583.

facts.statement: Paul Barrett and colleagues formally described the species as a new genus and species of sauropodomorph dinosaur in 2026.
facts.quote: In 2026, Paul Barrett and his colleagues described NHMZ 2583 as belonging to a new genus and species of sauropodomorph dinosaurs.

facts.statement: The genus name Musango honors the Musango Archosaur Site near the Musango Safari Camp on Lake Kariba where the fossil was found.
facts.quote: The generic name, Musango, refers to the Musango Archosaur Site within the Musango Concession Area near the Musango Safari Camp on the shores of Lake Kariba, Zimbabwe, where the holotype was recovered.

facts.statement: The species name matusadonaensis refers to the nearby Matusadona National Park.
facts.quote: The specific name, matusadonaensis, refers to Matusadona National Park, near the holotype locality.

facts.statement: Musango is the fifth dinosaur genus described from Zimbabwe.
facts.quote: Musango is the fifth genus of dinosaurs to be named from Zimbabwe

facts.statement: The animal lived during the Late Triassic epoch, specifically the Norian age.
Musango lived in the Upper Triassic (Norian) in the Pebbly Arkose Formation of Zimbabwe.
facts.quote: Musango is an extinct genus of unaysaurid sauropodomorph dinosaurs from the Upper Triassic (Norian) Pebbly Arkose Formation of Zimbabwe.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of a partial skeleton including dorsal and sacral vertebrae, ribs, shoulder bones, a forearm bone, a hand claw, hip bones, leg bones, ankle bones, and a toe bone.
facts.quote: The Musango holotype specimen consists of five dorsal (trunk) vertebrae, at least two sacral (hip) vertebrae, at least 15 caudal vertebrae, dorsal rib fragments, gastralia, three partial chevrons, a left scapula and coracoid (shoulder blade), an incomplete left humerus (forearm bone), a manual ungual (hand claw), a partial left ilium, a right pubis (hip bones), a partial right tibia and fibula (lower leg bones), the left astragalus and calcaneum (ankle bones), a left metatarsal, one pedal phalanx (toe bones), and various indeterminate bone fragments.

facts.statement: Based on comparisons with more complete relatives, researchers suggest Musango was likely an obligate biped.
facts.quote: Based on more complete relatives, Musango was likely an obligate biped.

facts.statement: Estimates based on the holotype suggest the animal reached a body length of about 4.5 meters and a mass of about 222 kilograms.
facts.quote: A holotype individual's body length was calculated at about 4.5 meters and its body mass was calculated at about 222 kilograms.

facts.statement: Musango is classified as a sauropodomorph belonging to the family Unaysauridae.
facts.quote: A sauropodomorph belonging to the family Unaysauridae.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places Musango in the clade Unaysauridae as the sister taxon to Musankwa.
facts.quote: This analysis placed Musango in the clade Unaysauridae, as the sister taxon to Musankwa.
